fields.description: Identifies the role of this site so Processa can behave appropriately per environment. "Review Doctypes/Workflow" is available only on a BA instance; "Reassign User Task" only on a Production instance.
fields.label: Instance Type

fields.description: Ex: https://one-fm.com
fields.label: Production URL

fields.description: If checked, a Process Implementation with "Active" status in Production is required to make changes to a process map.
fields.label: Connect to Production

fields.description: Ex: https://ba.one-fm.com
fields.label: BA Site URL

fields.description: Personal (or fine-grained) access token able to push branches and open pull requests. Used by "Review Doctypes" → "Sync" to raise a PR with the DocType schema changes, and by the Agent Sandbox when an agent opens a pull request. Needed on any instance that does either, production included — it does not depend on "Connect to Production".
fields.label: GitHub Access Token

fields.description: App whose source carries customizations made to other apps' DocTypes. A Custom Field on Employee belongs to this app, not to erpnext — so "Sync" writes it here, following this app's own convention (a data module under custom/custom_field/ plus custom/property_setter/, registered in setup/, applied by a patch). A DocType owned by an app that is itself a ONE-F-M repo is written to that app instead. Leave blank to fall back to the DocType's owning app.
fields.label: Customization Owner App

fields.description: App whose repository receives the pull request when the Connector Agent writes a Python handler for a connector operation. Most connectors need no code at all — an operation is normally a declarative HTTP request — but a signed request, walked pagination, or a call sequence needs a real function, and that function is delivered as a pull request rather than written into this site. Handlers land in connectors/generated/ in the named app, one module per connector, and the operation's Handler Path points at them. Defaults to the app that owns the connector layer. Leave blank to disable handler authoring entirely.
fields.label: Connector Handler App

fields.description: The AI Dev Agent: a Background agent delegated to over A2A that clones an app into an isolated Cloud Run sandbox, runs its real test suite, and delivers a passing change as a pull request via the same GitHub Integration above.
fields.label: Agent Sandbox

fields.description: Base URL of the deployed dev-agent-sandbox Cloud Run service for THIS environment (e.g. the beta service on a staging/BA site, the production service in production). Never point a non-production site at the production sandbox.
fields.label: Sandbox URL

fields.description: Shared HMAC secret verified against the sandbox's signed callback (X-Signature header). Must match the CALLBACK_HMAC_SECRET the sandbox was deployed with for this same environment — see deploy.py in the dev-agent-sandbox project.
fields.label: Callback Secret

fields.description: Full JSON key of the GCP service account used to mint the short-lived identity token that authenticates each dispatch call to the IAM-protected sandbox (Cloud Run Invoker role on that service). Paste the entire key file's contents here. Note: unlike site_config.json, this value travels with the database on backup/restore — granting a service account's key to a non-production environment (e.g. restoring a production backup onto staging) hands that environment the same Cloud Run Invoker access, so keep each environment's service account scoped to only the sandbox it should be allowed to call.
fields.label: Sandbox Caller Key (GCP Service Account JSON)

fields.description: Service account key the Chat Service Task sends with. Needs the chat.bot scope.
fields.label: Google Chat Service Account JSON

fields.description: Workspace account the directory lookup runs as. Empty falls back to matching on name.
fields.label: Directory Lookup Account

fields.options: Controls the pre-deployment security gate for BPMN Script Tasks. Dangerous escape vectors (exec/eval/getattr, frame-walking dunders, permission-bypass kwargs, memory bombs, destructive SQL) are always blocked and are not configurable here. The options below tighten the gate for constructs that also have legitimate uses; all default to allowed.

fields.description: Reject multiplication whose factor exceeds this value (memory-bomb guard, e.g. "A" * 999999999). Leave at 50000 unless you have a reason to change it.
fields.label: Multiplication Factor Threshold

fields.description: Block while loops in script tasks (use a BPMN gateway/loop instead).
fields.label: Block while Loops

fields.description: Block function definitions (def / async def) in script tasks.
fields.label: Block Function Definitions

fields.description: Block lambda expressions in script tasks.
fields.label: Block lambda Expressions

fields.description: Also block the commonly-legitimate builtins hasattr / type / id / classmethod / staticmethod.
fields.label: Strict Builtins

fields.description: Also block the sensitive Frappe attributes sql / commit / flags / conf / cache (destructive raw SQL is always blocked regardless).
fields.label: Strict Frappe Attributes

fields.description: Block ALL imports, not just the dangerous-module denylist.
fields.label: Block All Imports

fields.description: Who may release a frozen conversation. Site-wide because it is a statement about roles here, not about any one agent. The thresholds that DECIDE a freeze, and the message throttle, live on each AI Agent Configuration.
fields.label: AI Conversation Freeze

fields.description: Comma-separated roles allowed to release a frozen conversation. System Manager is always allowed. The locked user can never release their own conversation, whatever roles they hold.

Site-wide defaults for the models that write long-term memory and compact conversations. An agent's own Memory Models override these; with all blank, memory writes use the agent's own AI Model, exactly as before.
fields.label: AI Memory

fields.description: Used when an agent has no Distillation Model of its own.
fields.label: Default Distillation Model

fields.description: Used when an agent has no Reconciliation Model of its own. Tune here to fix poor reconciliations across every agent at once.
fields.label: Default Reconciliation Model

fields.description: Used when nothing else names a model for summarising the early part of a conversation. Summarising is high-volume and low-stakes, so this should be the cheap model — left blank, compaction uses whatever the caller passes and, failing that, does nothing rather than bill the agent's own reasoning model for it.
fields.label: Default Compaction Model

fields.description: Used when an agent sets no Context Token Budget of its own. Caps the assembled conversation history by estimated size, so a tool-heavy thread cannot outgrow the model's context window between compactions. 0 means no size limit.
fields.label: Default Context Token Budget

fields.description: Model that turns a memory into the numbers semantic search compares. Only models producing 384 numbers are listed, because that is the width of the stored column. Disabled turns semantic search off and leaves keyword search, which is what a machine that cannot download the model should use.
fields.label: Embedding Model
fields.options:
sentence-transformers/all-MiniLM-L6-v2
BAAI/bge-small-en-v1.5
snowflake/snowflake-arctic-embed-xs
snowflake/snowflake-arctic-embed-s
BAAI/bge-small-en
sentence-transformers/paraphrase-multilingual-MiniLM-L12-v2
Disabled

fields.description: Share of the memory search score that comes from meaning, from 0 to 1. The rest comes from keyword match. 1 ranks by meaning only, 0 by keywords only.
fields.label: Semantic Weight

fields.description: Share of the memory search score that comes from how recent the memory is, from 0 to 1. Recency halves every 30 days. What is left after recency and importance goes to relevance.
fields.label: Recency Weight

fields.description: Share of the memory search score that comes from the memory's Importance (1 to 5), from 0 to 1. What is left after recency and importance goes to relevance.
fields.label: Importance Weight

fields.description: Memory eval budget. How long a memory search may take, in milliseconds, before a Memory eval case fails on latency. Recall runs before every chat reply, so this is time added to each turn. Blank or 0 means 200.
fields.label: Retrieval Budget (ms)

fields.default:
User Statement
Agent Inference
Tool Output
fields.description: One source type per line, most trusted first. When a new memory contradicts an existing one, the higher source type wins; on a tie the higher effective confidence wins. Source types not listed rank lowest.
fields.label: Trust Hierarchy

fields.description: Nightly prune. A memory whose effective confidence (stored confidence halving every 90 days since it was last written or corroborated) falls under this is retired. 0 turns the rule off.
fields.label: Prune Below Confidence

fields.description: Nightly prune. A memory nothing has corroborated in this many days is retired. 0 turns the rule off.
fields.label: Prune Uncorroborated After Days

fields.description: Nightly prune. A never-corroborated memory with Importance 1 older than this many days is retired. 0 turns the rule off. Retired memories keep their row with the reason_retired filled in for auditing.
fields.label: Prune Minor Facts After Days

fields.description: Nightly audit. Raise an alert if one scope exceeds this many rows of memory. Use as a leading indicator of a memory that has diverged in the field (too many facts about too narrow a topic) or as a safety net if a memory eval fails to constrain scope. 0 means no alert.
fields.label: Alert When One Scope Exceeds

fields.description: Nightly audit. Raise an alert if the total number of memories exceeds this many rows. A broad leading indicator of memory accumulation. 0 means no alert.
fields.label: Alert When Total Rows Exceed

fields.description: Automatic deletion. After this many days (0 = never), move the conversation to the Archived folder and then delete its row so the index stays tight. Runs as a background job weekly.
fields.label: Conversation TTL (days)

fields.description: What to do with a TTL'd conversation: Archive it (move to the folder named Archived, deleting its row), or Delete it outright.
fields.label: Action on Expiry

fields.description: User Groups to alert if any AI Model's credentials are expiring or missing.
fields.label: Credential Alert Recipients

fields.description: User Groups to alert if an overnight eval run fails or spends over budget.
fields.label: Eval Alert Recipients

fields.description: The model used for the automated test grading in evals. When blank, defaults to gpt-4o.
fields.label: Nightly Eval Grading Model

fields.description: Daily maximum spend on overnight evals. When this is exceeded, any running eval is cancelled and not restarted. 0 means no limit.
fields.label: Nightly Eval Spend Ceiling

fields.description: Controls the amount of extra search context the OpenAI request includes. Low uses standard, Medium includes metadata, High includes full embeddings vectors (more tokens but better results). Empty falls back to Medium.
fields.label: OpenAI Search Context

fields.description: Observe AI conversations in LangSmith. Needs a LangSmith account and API key.
fields.label: Enable Observability

fields.description: Base URL of your Langfuse instance. Leave blank to skip Langfuse.
fields.label: Langfuse Base URL

fields.description: Public key for your Langfuse project.
fields.label: Langfuse Public Key

fields.description: Secret key for your Langfuse project.
fields.label: Langfuse Secret Key
